mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE spikes and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a single month signals a strong supply-side response, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate increased corporate profits and economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) signals a shift in consumer spending from goods to housing, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the housing sector strengthens.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases & RSAFS decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint behavior of HOUST and RSAFS does not significantly predict positive returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month period of CPIAUCSL inflation above 3% signals an overheating economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between high CPIAUCSL and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate increased consumer spending and economic growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases & UNRATE decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint behavior of PAYEMS and UNRATE does not significantly predict positive returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month period of negative real GDP growth (GDPC1) signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between negative GDPC1 growth and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
